neighbours.label: the word completing an emphatic set phrase: brand new, absolutely sure, half a dozen
fire: Our neighbours just moved into a brand new apartment on the far side of the park.
Last spring the school opened a brand new gym for its basketball teams.
Fans lined up overnight to get a look at the brand-new console and its games.
My uncle restored the engine until it looked brand new and ran without a sound.
Before you sign anything, be absolutely sure that the contract covers the repairs.
The pilot wanted to be absolutely sure about the weather ahead of the flight.
After the storm we found half a dozen broken branches lying across the driveway.
The bakery down the road sells half a dozen kinds of rye bread on weekends.
quiet: Our neighbours just moved into a new apartment on the far side of the park.
Last spring the school opened a larger gym for its basketball teams.
Fans lined up overnight to get a look at the latest console and its games.
My uncle restored the engine until it looked clean and ran without a sound.
Before you sign anything, be careful that the contract covers the repairs.
The pilot wanted to be well informed about the weather ahead of the flight.
After the storm we found several broken branches lying across the driveway.
The bakery down the road sells many kinds of rye bread on weekends.

notes: Probes: 'brand new' 0.24 against plain 'new' 0.006; 'absolutely sure' 0.39 against 'not sure' 0.14; 'half a dozen' 0.44. Other fixed phrases ('as a matter of fact', 'all of a sudden') stayed low, so this is not fixed phrases in general.
